extracted.intended_audience: readers of 19th-century American literature; theatre enthusiasts and students of acting
extracted.subtask_description: Prose-diary reminiscences and informal criticism focused on theatrical performance, actors, and poetry drawn from Walt Whitman's Specimen Days; mixes anecdote with evaluative observations about acting and poetic value. Useful for historical/theoretical insight rather than formal instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of passion in acting
rubrics_metrics.description: “instant and tremendous concentration of passion in his delineations overwhelm'd his audience, and wrought into it such enthusiasm that it partook of the fever of inspiration surging through his own veins.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance judged by an actor's ability to concentrate and transmit passionate intensity to the audience; exemplary effect cited is Edwin/Booth's power to overwhelm and inspire the house. Use sustained emotional focus to generate audience enthusiasm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneity and variability of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: “He was singularly spontaneous and fluctuating; in the same part each rendering differ'd from any and all others.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong performance avoids fixed, rehearsed gestures or stereotyped positions; each rendering should feel fresh and organically different. Anti-pattern: mechanical repetition or reliance on set poses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of stereotyped positions / freedom for fellow-performers
rubrics_metrics.description: “He had no stereotyped positions and made no arbitrary requirements on his fellow-performers.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good acting does not insist on rigid blocking that forces others into formulaic responses; it allows ensemble flexibility and spontaneity. Evaluate by how naturally the actor integrates with others without imposing artificial constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of stage points combined with naturalness
rubrics_metrics.description: “He knew all stage points thoroughly, and curiously ignored the mere dignities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical mastery (awareness of stage positions/points) is essential, but the best actors use that mastery without ostentation—prioritizing truthfulness over pomp. Scoring: technical competence plus understated, authentic use of technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to create and hold 'the hush' (timing and control)
rubrics_metrics.description: “I never saw an actor who could make more of the said hush or wait, and hold the audience in an indescribable, half-delicious, half-irritating suspense.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timing, silence, and the actor's capacity to build suspense and maintain audience attention through controlled pauses and beats. Example: Booth's entrances and pauses that arrested the house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage presence / visibility amid crowding
rubrics_metrics.description: “however crowded the stage might be, Booth never seem'd overtopt or hidden.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An actor's presence should command attention even in busy scenes—through posture, weighting, and focus—so they are neither lost nor overwhelmed. Assess by whether the audience's gaze naturally rests on the performer when intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliciting sustained audience attention and powerful response
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of Bowery audiences: paying 'sustain'd attention' and erupting in 'long-kept-up tempests of hand-clapping' and ovations for successful performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key success metric is audience engagement and visible response (sustained attention, ovations, palpable excitement). Examples cited include prolonged applause and visceral crowd reactions to Forrest and Booth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive valuation of poetic utterance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman's reflection: nearly five thousand poems and the idea that 'all poets, past and present, and of all poetic utterance' combine in an aggregate—'all poetry... have more features of resemblance than difference.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic criterion that emphasizes broad, inclusive appreciation of poetry across forms, eras, and languages—assessing poems in context of their contribution to the moral/esthetic progress of humanity rather than narrow technical conformity.
